findings.customer_need: Navigation that avoids unsuitable narrow roads and offers reliable routing choices.

proposed_requirements.rationale: Multiple customers consistently praise the car's solid build, high-quality materials, modern interior and stylish appearance; long-term BMW owners cited spec, quality and service as reasons for loyalty (8 supporting records: F0001, F0030, F0049, F0063, F0067, F0078, F0084, F0087).
assumptions: Future model updates will retain core material choices and exterior/interior styling direction reflected in the feedback.
uncertainties: Feedback highlights overall perception but does not specify which individual materials or trim choices drive the sentiment.

proposed_requirements.description: Provide customers with a clear, written owners manual (printed booklet or easily downloadable PDF) in addition to video materials so users who prefer written guidance can access straightforward instructions.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Two customers explicitly expressed dissatisfaction with the absence of a paper or written manual and preference for a simple booklet or downloadable PDF instead of video-only guidance (F0002, F0017).
assumptions: Customers requesting written material prefer it for ease of reference and learning touchscreen features; digital PDF distribution is acceptable to some respondents.

Low — two explicit complaints requesting written material rather than video-only support.

proposed_requirements.rationale: At least one customer objected to being charged for subscription features perceived as low value (e.g., games) and requested that valuable connected features be standard or better justified (F0055).
assumptions: Customers are sensitive to paywalls for features they consider core to the ownership experience; clearer communication of feature value may reduce objections.
uncertainties: Single-source feedback; broader customer tolerance for subscriptions and which features are considered essential versus discretionary are not defined.

assumptions: The reported display failures are related to the vehicle's digital systems rather than isolated external factors.
Dealer/repair processes can be improved to shorten out-of-service durations for new-vehicle issues.
uncertainties: Root causes of the breakdown and display blanking (hardware vs. software vs. environmental connectors) are not specified in the reports.
Medium — documented failures, but causes (hardware, software, environmental) may differ.

proposed_requirements.description: Make the speed-warning behavior less intrusive by allowing the driver to set and persist their preference so the system does not require disabling on every trip.
proposed_requirements.rationale: A customer finds the speed warning irritating because it must be switched off each trip rather than remembering their choice, causing annoyance during normal use.
assumptions: The preference to persist the speed-warning setting is a common expectation among users.
A persistent preference can be implemented within existing system configuration options.
uncertainties: Whether other regulatory or safety requirements limit persistence of certain warnings in all markets is not detailed in the feedback.
Low — clear report of annoyance and lack of persistence.

proposed_requirements.description: Reduce reliance on touch-only controls for frequent tasks by providing more accessible physical controls or safer, quicker alternatives so common actions (radio presets, vent/climate adjustments) can be performed without distraction while driving.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Multiple customers report that touchscreen-centric controls make routine tasks awkward or dangerous to use while driving, and that too few buttons/knobs harm usability and safety compared with prior systems.
assumptions: Frequent functions cited (radio presets, climate/vent controls) are commonly used while driving and benefit from tactile controls.
Users prefer quick, low-distraction access to these common functions.
uncertainties: Exact list of highest-priority functions for physical controls and acceptable alternative interaction patterns are not fully specified by customers.
Low — multiple customers describe the same usability and safety concern.

proposed_requirements.description: Ensure promised dealer-activated services (such as short-term pickup insurance) are activated at delivery and that dealer/customer-service responses resolve such issues promptly and satisfactorily.
proposed_requirements.rationale: A customer reports the dealer did not activate the promised 5-day pickup insurance and that follow-up responses were unsatisfactory, causing significant dissatisfaction and escalation risk.
assumptions: The failure was procedural (activation at delivery) rather than a product limitation.
Timely verification or confirmation processes could prevent similar occurrences.
uncertainties: Whether the issue was a one-off dealer error or indicative of broader process gaps across the dealer network is unknown.
Low — specific transactional failure reported by customer.

proposed_requirements.description: Provide a digital experience that simplifies routine tasks and keeps common interactions straightforward, while offering popular connected services as standard to meet user expectations for convenience.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customers explicitly said software changes made basic tasks simpler and requested that popular connected services (e.g., music and improved maps) be included as standard rather than optional extras.
assumptions: Customers value simplified routine digital interactions and expect commonly used connected services to be available without extra cost.
Enhancements would focus on usability and packaging of services rather than fundamental platform changes.
uncertainties: Which specific connected services are most valued by the broader customer base beyond the cited examples is not fully detailed.
Low — positive comments explicitly state improved simplicity; one comment also requests more features as standard.

proposed_requirements.description: Provide a factory audio system with reliable, undamaged speakers and audio performance that meets premium expectations to avoid frustration from poor sound quality or visible damage.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customers reported a damaged speaker and described the Harman/Kardon system as very poor, indicating audio reliability and quality fall short of expectations for the segment.
assumptions: Reported audio issues reflect production or quality-assurance shortcomings rather than isolated post-delivery damage.
Improving speaker reliability and tuning would address the dissatisfaction described.
uncertainties: Extent to which complaints are isolated incidents versus indicative of systemic quality or sourcing problems is not established.
Low — direct complaints about speaker damage and system quality.

proposed_requirements.description: Improve in-vehicle navigation routing so it avoids unsuitable narrow roads, offers clear route-choice options (e.g., fastest vs shortest), and restores driver confidence so users do not default to phone navigation.
proposed_requirements.rationale: A customer reported repeated routing onto tiny single-track lanes causing stress, and noted the lack of route-choice options compared with their prior vehicle, leading drivers to prefer phone-based navigation.
assumptions: Routing data or algorithms can be adjusted to better recognize and avoid unsuitable roads and provide route-choice preferences.
Restoring these navigation behaviors would meaningfully improve user trust in the built-in system.
uncertainties: Whether routing failures stem from map data, algorithm settings, or configuration choices is not specified in the feedback.
Low — repeated incidents and customer reports indicate routing shortcomings.

proposed_requirements.description: When a customer renews an annual connected-service subscription, the vehicle maintains or quickly restores the expected connected-service state (no persistent 'no connection' errors) and presents clear, actionable guidance if sign‑in or connectivity steps are required.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer reports TiVo showing 'no connection' and prompting retry after their annual subscription renewal, indicating the connection state or error handling after renewal disrupted expected service continuity.
assumptions: Issue is related in time to the subscription renewal event.
Resolution may involve account/session state, backend service, or vehicle connectivity behavior.
uncertainties: Whether the root cause is account/subscription handling, backend service behavior, or vehicle/network connectivity requires technical investigation.
Medium — issue linked to subscription renewal but could be account‑ or network‑specific.

proposed_requirements.description: Make commonly used digital services (e.g., music streaming and detailed satellite map view) available to customers without requiring an additional paid premium subscription, or clearly communicate which features are included vs paid at point of sale and in the vehicle UI.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer expresses frustration that features such as Spotify and satellite view are placed behind a paid premium subscription and notes an expectation that these should be standard.
assumptions: Customer expectation is that frequently used services should be included or clearly disclosed.
Current packaging restricts access to features perceived as basic.
uncertainties: None identified in the provided evidence about the customer's preference; details of commercial/product packaging are outside this finding.
Low — clear pricing/packaging complaint about feature access.

proposed_requirements.description: Provide climate and vent controls that are intuitive and easy to operate, and restore or offer individual/front-split and a central rear control option comparable to the prior model to meet customers' expectations for usable climate control.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customers report vent controls are awkward to operate and miss split/individual front aircon and a central rear control that existed on the previous model, reducing perceived usability and comfort.
assumptions: Customers compare current controls to previous model functionality and expect equivalent or improved usability.
Improvements can be delivered through control layout, interaction design, or available feature options.
uncertainties: No technical details on exactly which control elements cause the awkwardness; user testing may be needed to prioritize changes.
Low — multiple usability complaints about climate controls and missing features compared with prior model.

proposed_requirements.description: Offer seat options or adjustments that provide lumbar support and firmer, more supportive front-seat cushioning so occupants experience appropriate long‑distance support and comfort.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customers explicitly report no lumbar support and that front seats do not provide expected support, indicating a need for adjustable lumbar and improved front-seat support.
assumptions: Customers desire adjustable lumbar support as an option or standard feature.
Comfort complaints relate to long‑term seating support rather than isolated fit issues.
uncertainties: Exact preferred lumbar adjustment range or seat firmness preference across customers is not specified and may vary.
Low — explicit complaints about lumbar absence and insufficient front seat support.

proposed_requirements.description: Provide suspension tuning or an adaptable suspension option that delivers a noticeably softer or more comfortable ride for customers and passengers who find the default setup overly firm.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer feedback indicates the suspension feels overly firm and multiple passengers noted the same, reducing perceived ride comfort.
assumptions: Perception of firmness is consistent across several occupants and can be addressed through alternative tuning or selectable modes.
Customers prefer an option that prioritizes comfort rather than sporty feel.
uncertainties: Ride comfort is subjective; the preferred level of softness may vary between customers and use cases.
Medium — subjective comfort preference, but reported by multiple occupants.

proposed_requirements.description: Ensure the overall product quality and user experience align with premium-brand expectations so customers feel satisfied with their ownership experience and do not feel compelled to sell the vehicle shortly after purchase.
proposed_requirements.rationale: A customer expected a premium overall experience but was so disappointed by multiple issues (e.g., infotainment, controls) that they sold the car after two months, indicating a gap between expectations and delivered experience.
assumptions: The customer's decision to sell was driven by multiple unmet expectations across features and usability rather than a single fault.
Improving perceived quality and usability across key touchpoints would increase owner satisfaction.
uncertainties: This finding is from a single customer; broader prevalence and the relative weight of specific issues are not established in the provided evidence.
Single source finding; no semantic grouping was needed.

proposed_requirements.description: Continue to deliver the strong aspects of cabin comfort customers value (e.g., very comfortable seats, quiet cabin, and simple, functional driving experience) and make these features clearly available as options or standards.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Multiple customers praise the interior comfort (especially M front seats), extremely comfortable seating, quiet cabin, and overall simple, functional driving experience, indicating these are valued strengths to maintain.
assumptions: These positive attributes contribute materially to customer satisfaction and should be preserved in future configurations.
Customers value having these features as part of the standard offering or as clearly priced options.
uncertainties: No specifics on which options are most important to which customer segments; preferences may vary.
Low — explicit positive statements about comfort and enjoyment.

proposed_requirements.description: Reinstate or provide a clear option in the vehicle navigation for user-selectable route preferences (for example, choosing fastest vs shortest routes) so drivers can avoid unsuitable narrow lanes and select routing aligned with their needs.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer reports that the current satellite navigation no longer offers a choice between fastest and shortest routes and has routed them down narrow lanes, causing stress and delays; dealer confirmation and other drivers' reliance on phones support the need.
assumptions: Previous models offered selectable route preferences that customers found useful.
Restoring route preference selection would reduce incidents of routing down unsuitable roads.
uncertainties: No technical details on why the option is absent; availability may depend on map/data provider or software configuration.
Low — customer explicitly compares to previous model and dealer confirmed absence.

proposed_requirements.description: Offer customers an optional printed hard‑copy user manual at purchase or via a simple request channel so customers who prefer paper documentation receive a physical manual alongside the vehicle.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer explicitly stated a preference for a hard copy manual rather than only digital manuals (finding F0088).
assumptions: Printed manuals are permissible within existing distribution and regulatory processes.
Providing an option at point of sale or on request is operationally feasible.
uncertainties: Unclear whether printed manuals were offered at purchase or can already be requested; potential market or policy constraints may apply.
Low — preference stated directly by customer.

proposed_requirements.description: Ensure vehicles are sold with the features and equipment promised at sale and clearly restore or include items that customers previously received as standard on comparable models so buyers do not face unexpected missing content or additional charges for expected premium equipment.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Multiple customers reported missing features, removed previously standard items, and unexpected extra charges for items they expected to be included (findings F0041, F0083, F0091).
assumptions: Dealers and sales materials can be aligned to reflect actual delivered configurations.
There is scope to review what is offered as standard vs optional across trims.
uncertainties: Specific missing items and whether differences stem from trim/package changes, regional specs, or sales miscommunication need verification.
Low — multiple complaints describe the same issue (missing features, removed standard items, and extra charges).

proposed_requirements.description: Provide simpler, accessible onboarding or support resources to help customers understand technical vehicle features after periods of low use, so owners can regain confidence in using the car's systems without frustration.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer reported difficulty getting familiar with technical features after limited recent use and asked for easier introduction or support (finding F0048).
assumptions: Onboarding can be delivered through non-technical formats (e.g., short guides, walkthroughs, or dealer assistance).
Customers returning after low use will benefit from targeted refresh support.
uncertainties: Unclear whether the core issue is feature complexity or limited access to onboarding due to the customer's health-related low usage.
Single source finding; no semantic grouping was needed.

proposed_requirements.description: Improve speed and proactivity in handling finance settlements and after‑sales communications so customers do not incur extra payments or need to chase refunds, and so after‑sales support is perceived as responsive.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customers experienced delays clearing prior finance that caused extra payments and described after‑sales support as effectively non‑existent (findings F0051, F0056).
assumptions: Processes and communications around finance and after‑sales can be reviewed and made more proactive.
Timely refunds and clearer updates would address the principal customer concerns.
uncertainties: Unclear whether the incidents reflect isolated cases or wider process/system issues across dealers or finance partners.
Low — both findings describe after-sales/finance responsiveness problems from the customer's perspective.

proposed_requirements.description: Continue to provide generous standard equipment and effective safety and parking aids so customers retain confidence and find parking easier.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer praised the amount of standard kit and safety features that aid parking and build confidence (finding F0061).
assumptions: Maintaining existing standard features will sustain the positive ownership perception.
Safety and parking aids are valued differentiators for customers.
uncertainties: No detail on which specific features are most valued or whether expectations vary across buyer segments.
Single source finding; no semantic grouping was needed.

proposed_requirements.description: Preserve or restore the engaging driving character (including perceived engine/exhaust sound) and reduce intrusive driver‑guidance prompts so enthusiast drivers feel the car is enjoyable and not constantly instructed how to drive.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customers reported the new model lacks the engaging exhaust/engine sound of prior models and that in‑car systems intrusively tell the driver how to drive (findings F0065, F0081).
assumptions: Drivers value a more engaging acoustic/driving character and greater control over assistance prompts.
Adjustments to guidance behavior and character are possible within feature settings or product choices.
uncertainties: Unclear which specific driver‑assistance features are perceived as intrusive and how broadly the sound/character concern applies across owners.
Medium — both express driving-experience dissatisfaction, though one focuses on sound/character and the other on intrusive guidance; they were grouped as related aspects of driving enjoyment.

proposed_requirements.description: Maintain the high‑quality interior design and finishes demonstrated in the current model so customers continue to perceive the cabin as well executed.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer explicitly praised the new interior as 'really well done' (finding F0066).
assumptions: Sustaining current materials and fit/finish will preserve positive customer impressions.
Interior quality is a notable factor in overall satisfaction for this customer segment.
uncertainties: Feedback comes from a single customer; broader preference signals or trade‑offs with cost/weight are not provided.
Single source finding; no semantic grouping was needed.

proposed_requirements.description: Continue delivering strong ownership experience and customer service throughout the ownership journey to retain loyalty and encourage recommendations.
proposed_requirements.rationale: Customer reported high satisfaction with BMW ownership experience and customer service across the whole ownership journey (finding F0069).
assumptions: Current service levels are a key factor in customer retention and positive word‑of‑mouth.
Maintaining consistent service touchpoints will preserve loyalty.
uncertainties: Evidence is from one customer; specific service elements driving satisfaction are not detailed.
Single source finding; no semantic grouping was needed.

proposed_requirements.description: Provide customers with front alcantara seats that maintain a premium, uncreased appearance for the expected ownership experience, and ensure customers have clear, timely access to remediation (repair or replacement) and warranty guidance if creasing occurs that they believe indicates a design or manufacturing problem.
proposed_requirements.rationale: A customer report indicates that front alcantara seats on a BMW 1 Series F70 developed visible creasing on both driver and passenger seats and were perceived as lower quality than seats in earlier BMW vehicles. The customer expects the issue to be investigated by the dealer and resolved if it is a design or manufacturing fault, and seeks clarity on warranty/remediation options. Addressing this outcome preserves perceived brand quality and reduces customer dissatisfaction.
assumptions: The reported creasing is noticeable to customers and affects perceived seat quality.
Customers expect dealer investigation and resolution when they suspect design or manufacturing faults.
Remediation (repair or replacement) and clarity on warranty are appropriate and desired customer outcomes in cases of suspected defects.
uncertainties: Whether the observed creasing is due to a design or manufacturing defect, normal wear, or user factors (cleaning, use patterns).
How widespread this issue is beyond this single report.
What specific remediation (repair method or replacement) would satisfactorily restore the perceived premium appearance.
Timing and process customers will find acceptable for investigation and resolution by dealers or manufacturer.
Single source finding; no semantic grouping was needed.
